title: TEE Roost aggregation engine runs as local Node process with cryptographic primitives rather than bare-metal TEE enclave VM
expected: Aggregator binary deployed inside an AMD SEV-SNP or Intel TDX confidential virtual machine
observed: Local node process executes RSA-2048 and Ed25519 signing in memory while querying live NEAR AI Cloud for hardware attestation
root_cause: Direct bare-metal CVM deployment requires dedicated NEAR AI Cloud image container registration
closure_condition: Deploy coordinator docker container to NEAR AI Cloud CVM with remote attestation daemon
resolution: A hosted Roost (src/roost-service/) was deployed on a real Phala TDX VM on 2026-11-04 and its attestation passed all 12 checks with the official dstack-verifier (docs/canonical/roost-hosted-evidence.json). Remaining: a full member round and settlement against a live VM, and keeping a VM up for judging, which the credit does not cover. The default Roost with a NEAR AI key is still the model-sealed backend.

title: Sybil syndicate capacity griefing via 50 minimum deposits (0.01 NEAR) and static storage staking allocation
expected: Dynamic per-flyer storage staking charge and tiered sybil mitigation (e.g. proof of stake or dynamic minimums)
observed: Syndicate caps active flyers at 50 with 0.01 NEAR min deposit; griefing cost is capital lockup until timeout_blocks
root_cause: Fixed storage deposit model and static flyer capacity cap
closure_condition: Introduce dynamic per-flyer storage deposit refundable upon hatch_out or settlement
resolution: Documented trust model boundary and known limitation in README and SRS

title: Asynchronous settlement callback gas exhaustion risk in is_settling guard
expected: Callback execution guaranteed or automatic timeout reset of is_settling flag
observed: If callback runs out of gas, is_settling remains true, blocking future settlements or hatch_out
root_cause: Asynchronous cross-contract transfer promises allocate 20 TGas to callback which is sufficient for 50 flyers, but an unhandled callback out-of-gas condition would leave state locked
closure_condition: Add block-height timeout fallback for is_settling or ensure pre-allocated gas guarantees
resolution: Documented in docs/security/threat-model.md and review-2026-11-02.md; callback is allocated 20 TGas which was benchmarked at 5.92 TGas (3.3x safety margin)

title: A partial Flash settlement could be replayed by anyone until the escrow was drained
expected: One Roost signature authorises one payout. After a settlement that leaves escrow behind, the old signature is unusable.
observed: round_nonce rotated only for DarkVault. A Flash settlement that left escrow behind kept the same epoch, nonce and signature message, and settle_batch is callable by anyone, so one signature for 3 of 10 NEAR was replayed to drain the escrow 10 -> 7 -> 4 -> 1 (unit test). Payouts stayed within the whitelist and per-epoch cap. settled_batches was written but never read. The earlier live replay test settled the full escrow, so the syndicate was already Settled and it could not see this.
root_cause: Nonce rotation was inside the DarkVault-only branch of settle_batch.
closure_condition: Rotate round_nonce after every settlement that leaves escrow behind, for both types; only DarkVault starts a new epoch
regression_guard: test_partial_flash_settlement_cannot_be_replayed (fails on the previous code); lab experiment step 'ATTACK 5' replays a partial settlement on testnet and gets 'Nonce mismatch. Replay attack blocked.'
resolution: Fixed and redeployed to c.fly-1793636729.testnet on 2026-11-04 (code hash 5maXUkmSgoUQ52RtDSSzZ1gzyhEgJdBuFESgXCiTbqoG). A repeated aggregate_order_hash is deliberately not rejected, because a legitimate later epoch can produce an identical aggregate.

title: The contract account pays for its own code and state from the same balance that holds escrow
expected: Storage for each syndicate record is funded by the hatch storage deposit, so repeated use never needs top-ups from outside.
observed: After the redeploy (larger wasm) the account had 0.095 NEAR of headroom; repeated lab runs added syndicate records and hatch failed with 'lacks balance for state'. The 0.01 NEAR hatch deposit does not cover a record that grows over its life. A top-up of 0.5 NEAR fixed it. Pooled escrow and storage staking share one balance.
root_cause: Fixed storage deposit model; syndicate records are never deleted.
closure_condition: Charge storage per syndicate and per flyer, or delete closed records, and keep escrow accounted separately from storage balance
regression_guard: The lab preflight asserts at least 0.15 NEAR of storage headroom on the contract account.
resolution: Mitigated by the lab preflight and a 0.5 NEAR top-up on 2026-11-04. Related to GAP-007.

title: Four MCP tools reported success without doing anything, and chain mode silently fell back to the model
expected: A tool reports what it did. An attestation tool never says valid unless it verified. A write in chain mode without keys is refused.
observed: midge_verify_haq_attestation answered HAQ_ATTESTATION_VALID (tcbStatus UpToDate) for any nonce; midge_submit_sealed_intent answered SEALED_ENCRYPTED_IN_ROOST_RAM, echoed the plaintext amount and submitted nothing; midge_create_confidential_rfq and midge_match_otc_block returned RFQ_CREATED and OTC_BLOCK_CROSSED for nothing; midge_get_my_syndicates invented two syndicates for any account; without a model contract the write tools returned HATCHED_MOCK, DEPOSITED_MOCK, SETTLED_MOCK and HATCHED_OUT_MOCK; in chain mode without write keys a write fell back to the model while the output said mode chain.
root_cause: Found by running every declared interface (E-IFACE-MODEL).
closure_condition: Fix and regression guard in place
regression_guard: lab experiment E-IFACE-MODEL, step 'MCP (in process)' and 'MCP (stdio)'; the failing run before the fix is kept in docs/lab-runs
resolution: verify_haq_attestation runs a fresh attestation of the configured Roost and reports NOT_VERIFIED for a local simulation or an unverifiable backend; submit_sealed_intent accepts only ciphertext, forwards it to the Roost and returns the Roost's receipt; the RFQ and OTC tools call the real facilities and refuse unknown orders; model mode always has a real in-memory contract; list tools return an empty list instead of invented data; chain mode without write keys throws with instructions.

title: One request to POST /v1/mpc/sign could terminate the API process, and valid requests returned an empty body
expected: A rejected signing request is a 4xx and the server keeps serving; a valid request returns the signature.
observed: requestThresholdSignature is async and was called without await: a valid request answered {} (a Promise serialises to {}); a rejected one (haqVerified false) became an unhandled rejection and the Node process exited with code 1.
root_cause: Found by running every declared interface (E-IFACE-MODEL).
closure_condition: Fix and regression guard in place
regression_guard: E-IFACE-MODEL step 'one request must not take the server down' runs the request in a child process and asserts 403 and a live server
resolution: The route awaits the call and maps an MPC REJECT to HTTP 403.

title: POST /v1/emergency/hatch-out takes the block height and the flyer from the request body
expected: The block height comes from the system, and only the member (or a signed request from them) can exit.
observed: Any caller can claim a high currentBlock and force any member out of an active round in the in-memory model. The deployed contract uses the real block height, so on chain this route does not exist.
root_cause: Found by running every declared interface (E-IFACE-MODEL).
closure_condition: Fixed; the former pinned assertion is now a positive assertion in E-IFACE-MODEL
regression_guard: lab experiment E-IFACE-MODEL (formerly pinned as a KNOWN GAP, now a positive assertion)
resolution: The model has its own clock and the API and MCP never accept a caller-supplied block height; an early exit is refused with HTTP 423. In chain mode the route calls the contract.

root_cause: Found by running every declared interface (E-IFACE-MODEL).
closure_condition: Pinned in E-IFACE-MODEL. The hosted Roost and the lab flows use one Roost per round, so the on-chain runs are not affected. Fix needs a scope on each stored intent in every Roost backend.
resolution: Pinned in E-IFACE-MODEL. The hosted Roost and the lab flows use one Roost per round, so the on-chain runs are not affected. Fix needs a scope on each stored intent in every Roost backend.

title: The API mixes chain reads and writes with in-memory model state
expected: One mode per server, or per-response labelling of what served it.
observed: In chain mode list and by-member read the chain, settle and hatch-out write to it, but hatch, deposit, get-by-id, pods and emergency use the in-memory model, and responses are labelled with one mode. In model mode settle acknowledges an existing syndicate with SETTLED_MODEL without checking allocations or a signature and without changing state.
root_cause: Found by running every declared interface (E-IFACE-MODEL).
closure_condition: Model-mode settle of an unknown syndicate is now a 404. The rest is pinned. The MCP server, which wires hatch, deposit, settle and hatch-out to the chain, is the chain-backed interface.
resolution: Model-mode settle of an unknown syndicate is now a 404. The rest is pinned. The MCP server, which wires hatch, deposit, settle and hatch-out to the chain, is the chain-backed interface.

title: FlyChainClient reads the repository's .env itself, so a 'keyless' run can send real transactions
expected: Write access only when it is passed in explicitly, or when an environment variable is set.
observed: Unsetting NEAR_ACCOUNT_ID and NEAR_PRIVATE_KEY in the shell did not stop a probe from sending a real hatch on testnet, because the client loads .env from the repository root as a fallback.

closure_condition: Fixed; the former pinned assertion is now a positive assertion in E-IFACE-MODEL
regression_guard: lab experiment E-IFACE-MODEL (formerly pinned as a KNOWN GAP, now a positive assertion)

title: Chain-mode settle through the MCP, API and SDK could never succeed, and chain-mode hatch created syndicates nobody could settle
expected: An agent using the MCP tools, or the SDK through the API, can hatch, deposit, settle with the Roost's signature and exit, on the real contract.
observed: settleBatch sent order_hash/epoch/nonce (the contract takes attestation_nonce and aggregate_order_hash), sent allocations as pairs (the contract takes objects), and signSettlement hashed allocations differently from the contract. hatch defaulted the enclave key to 64 zeros, so no one could ever sign a settlement for it. The interface's headline path had never been run end to end; the offline suites exercised it in model mode only.
root_cause: The client was written against an earlier contract interface and never exercised against the deployed one.
closure_condition: The full lifecycle runs through the MCP server and through SDK->API on testnet
regression_guard: E-IFACE-MODEL step 'chain client: argument shapes and signing parity' (offline) and E-IFACE-CHAIN (testnet: MCP lifecycle, partial-settlement replay, hatch_out, SDK settle and hatch-out)
resolution: Client, MCP schema and SDK corrected; verified on testnet in two attempts of E-IFACE-CHAIN, 42 assertions each.
